ety.text: From Middle English us, from Old English ūs (“us”, dative personal pronoun), from Proto-West Germanic *uns, from Proto-Germanic *uns (“us”), from Proto-Indo-European *n̥swé, alteration of *n̥smé (“us”). The compensatory lengthening was lost in Middle English due to the word being unstressed when used. Cognate with Saterland Frisian uus (“us”), West Frisian us, ús (“us”), Low German uns, us (“us”), Dutch ons (“us”), German uns (“us”), Danish os (“us”), Latin nōs (“we, us”).

senses.d: Me and at least one other person, excluding the person(s) being addressed. (exclusive us.)
Me and at least one other person, including the person(s) being addressed. (inclusive us.)
ex: Let's ask him if he'll give us a lift.
Forasmuch as many have taken in hand to set forth in order a declaration of those things which are most surely believed among us...

senses.d: We, used in the same circumstances where “me” would be used instead of “I”, e.g. for the pronoun in isolation or as the complement of the copula
ex: Who's going to go? — Us. We'll go.

senses.d: Any entity that the speaker is a part of or identifies with, such as place of employment or education, nation, region, language, etc.
ex: It's not true that the rest of Europe hates us.
I went to watch my favourite team play Real Madrid, but they thrashed us 5-0.
Come on! Wakey wakey! Let's get us up and out of bed, please.

senses.d: Used to imply connection between the speaker's experiences or activities and a group of listeners.
ex: Hey guys, in this video I'll show you how I make my upside-down sponge cake. First let's get us a few ingredients that we'll need ...
Give us a look at your paper.
Fetch us a cold beer from the fridge, would you.
Look at us while ye’re speakin tiv us.
Could ye dee that for us?

senses.d: Designates the speaker(s)/writer(s) as constituting or belonging to the stated category of people (objective case).
ex: It's not good enough for us teachers.

senses.d: Designates the speaker(s)/writer(s) as constituting or belonging to the stated category of people (subjective case).
ex: Us gays and lesbians in here got a reason to be bitching about the conditions.
We'll have to throw us food out.

senses.d: The relationship between the speaker and some other unspecified person.
ex: Us is the best thing that's ever happened to me.

ety.text: Inherited from Old Spanish nos (“us”) (from Latin nōs) + otros (“others”) (plural of otro, from Latin alter). Compare Galician nosoutros, Catalan nosaltres, Occitan nosautres, French nous autres, Friulian noaltris, Italian noialtri.
